note: Certified questions whose span was cut short by a sentence splitter that read an INITIAL as a sentence end. The truncation is a SEGMENTATION defect, not a classification one: every row here was already certified as a Question, on the right drop, with the right count. What was wrong is where the span stopped.
why: Q writes "H. Biden", "A. Merkel", "N. Korea", "U.S. Supreme Court". A splitter that ends a sentence at "." cuts the question at the initial, so #4898 was certified as "Why is the FBI's top child porn lawyer involved in the H." and painted only that far - the reader saw a question mark on screen with no blue under it. Recorded here rather than fixed in the deriving audit, for the same reason every other owner overlay is: a correction written into a re-derivable artifact is erased the next time its audit runs.
rule: The full span is taken FROM THE DROP, never retyped: the drop line that starts with the truncated text, run to its terminal "?". #4891's second row ends in a period instead, which is Q's habit and which the certified question form has always accepted.
provenance: owner ruling on #4898, 2026-08-21 - "this should be a full question but is partially highlighted". The other nine are the same defect, found by sweeping every certified question ending in an initial.

withdrawn.note: The SAME splitter emitted the tail of each broken question as a certified question of its own. Repairing the head without withdrawing the tail leaves one sentence certified twice - once whole, once as a fragment - which is the same-category overlap the owner ruled against on 2026-08-21. The fragment is absorbed into the full span, not deleted from the archive: it is the same words, counted once.
